answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a bonded identity registry. Each agent locks a crystal stake and presents a unique signed attestation; the yarrow rule slashes the entire bond if two identities share a key or device. That attestation is a cheap signal of uniqueness any peer can verify. To mint N fake workers an attacker must post N separate bonds and forge N independent attestations, so cost grows linearly, and every caught duplicate burns the stake. With each bond worth more than the rewards a fake agent can earn, Sybil farming becomes a guaranteed loss.
